```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(BSDA)
```


#### **Q1. Normality test / Prueba de normalidad**
```{r}
butterflies <- read_excel("butterflies_pesticides.xlsx")
head(butterflies)
```
```{r}
table(butterflies$Group)
```


```{r}
shapiro.test(butterflies$'Wing Length' [butterflies$Group=="group1"])
```


```{r}
shapiro.test(butterflies$'Wing Length' [butterflies$Group=="group2"])
```





#### **Q2. Equality of variances test / Prueba de igualdad de varianzas**
```{r}
var.test(butterflies$'Wing Length'~butterflies$Group)
```


#### **Q3. Statistical test / Prueba estadística**
```{r}
t.test(filter(butterflies, Group=="group1")$'Wing Length',
       filter(butterflies, Group=="group2")$'Wing Length',
       alternative="two.sided",
       mu=0,
       paired=FALSE,
       var.equal=FALSE)
```


#### **Q4. ggplot**
```{r}
ggplot(butterflies, aes(x=Group, y=`Wing Length`)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Butterfly Wing Length by Pesticide Treatment",
       x="Treatment Group",
       y="Wing Lenght")
```


#### **Q5. Summary paragraph / Párrafo de resumen**
##### We examine whether pesticide exposure during the larval stage affects butterfly wing length by comparing 40 pesticide treated butterflies (group 2) with 40 untreated butterflies (group 1). Shapiro-Wilk tests indicated that both group were approximately normally distributed (p=0.146 and p=0.6247). An F-test showed significant difference in variance between the groups (p=0.005512). We used a two-tailed independent t-test to compare their mean wing lengths. The results showed statistically significant difference between the groups (t=3.9832, df=66.029, p=0.0001721). Untreated butterflies had a higher mean wing length (632.18) than pesticide treated butterflies (593.49). These findings suggest that pesticide exposure during larval stage may negatively impact butterfly wing development.
